newsitem.title: FINLAND: FINNISH BUILDING SUBCONTRACTORS UP AS PICK-UP SEEN.
newsitem.headline: FINNISH BUILDING SUBCONTRACTORS UP AS PICK-UP SEEN.

text.p: Finnish hardware retailer Starckjohann Oy and construction machinery leasing company Rakentajain Konevuokraamo Oy rose in active trade on Wednesday, bolstered by brighter building prospects, brokers said.
At 1305/1105 GMT, Starckjohann traded at a year-high 8.55 markka, up 0.25 markka or three percent. Turnover was particularly lively for Starckjohann at 3.5 million markka.
OTC-listed Rakentajain Konevuokraamo was up 1.20 markka, also three percent, at 41.20 markka. Volume was moderate.
Brokers said both companies were boosted by news that Swedish construction group Skanska will build an apartment block worth 750 million crowns (about 503 million markka) in Helsinki.
Operators said there was a fundamental upward trend in construction sector shares as building prospects have picked up.
"As the outloook for the (construction) sector has clearly improved -- construction materials sales growth is likely to exceed the average growth in sales," Opstock analyst Jukka Linden said.
Liquidity in Starckjohann shares improved after Yrityspankki SKOP sold over 16 percent of its stake in the company on January 10, brokers said.
